item.title: Oklahoma Insurance Investigation Leads to $45M State Farm Settlement
item.description: will pay a $45 million settlement after a state insurance department investigation found it failed to properly pay roof damage claims by Oklahoma customers. The state’s incoming insurance commissioner, Republican Bob Sullivan, said he was still learning details on Friday but worried the settlement may take some flexibility out of any regulatory approach to State Farm under his administration. State Farm is Oklahoma’s top homeowners insurer, with more than 258,000 customers and $785.9 million in homeowners premiums in 2025.

item.title: Nvidia, Board Still Face Legal Risks After Huang’s Return
item.description: Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO at the urging of US President Donald Trump, less than two weeks after the co-founder of the AI chip powerhouse resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China. Nvidia said in a statement that based on US government input the board was confident that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” a claim backed by Trump in an interview with CNBC. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia to make repeated assurances about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, until the allegations were public.

item.title: Coastal Storms Could Put a Damper on Thanksgiving Plans
item.description: Storms across the Southeast and along the West Coast will bring scattered showers and thunderstorms, while chillier air around the Mississippi Valley could also bring snow and rain just in time to snarl Wednesday travel plans, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). A West Coast storm brings along the chance of more high tides which could lead to coastal flooding. A strong Thanksgiving Day storm threatens the Ohio Valley to the Eastern Seaboard, bringing with it windy conditions, heavy rain, and flooding risk.

item.title: How should investors evaluate performance?
item.description: Before selling a fund that has underperformed its benchmark, investors should ask why and whether it still meets their needs. So, the first question isn’t simply: ‘Did this fund beat the market?’ Instead, investors should ask: ‘Is this fund fulfilling its intended role?’ That means looking at its stated objective, strategy and style (for example, whether it invests in particular countries or sectors, or favours value or growth companies). Investors should also consider the portfolio’s overall balance of risk and return and the timeframe for assessing results.

item.title: Reinsurance renewals running later than usual, focus remains largely on price: Althoff, Hannover Re
item.description: Sven Althoff, Member of the Executive Board for Property & Casualty at Hannover Re, explained this morning that the reinsurance renewals are running later than usual in many areas and while rate adequacy is expected for many parts of the portfolio, he acknowledged there may be a need to start cycle managing due to price pressures. Speaking during the Hannover Re investor day held in London today, Althoff said that with the January 2027 renewals running behind their typical end of year schedule, it means data points are still lacking as to how much rates may move at 1/1. Althoff explained that as the January 2027 reinsurance renewals approach, pressure on the pricing environment continues to be seen, echoing what was discussed with Hannover Re’s clients at the Monte Carlo event in September.

item.description: “But, especially with HCP, Hannover Re Capital Partners, quite huge interest from investors to connect our nat cat business with third-party capital, so we are on a good journey on that.” Sehm later explained that Hannover Re’s corporate strategy shows priorities are accessing risk, evaluating risk and transforming risk, with the ILS business highly relevant strategically. item.title: Oliver Wyman names Netherton as Global Head & Moloney as Executive Chair, Insurance & Asset Management
item.description: Oliver Wyman, a global management consulting firm and a Marsh business, has promoted George Netherton as Global Head of Insurance and Asset Management (IAM), effective immediately. He succeeds Michael Moloney, who will transition to Executive Chair of Insurance and Asset Management while maintaining leadership roles in risk and insurance consulting at Oliver Wyman Actuarial and Marsh Risk. item.title: How Will This Year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Weather the Storm?
item.description: The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is set for Thursday morning in New York City, but gusty winds and periods of heavy rain in the forecast could keep its famous giant character balloons close to the ground. Under New York City safety rules, 34 mph is the maximum wind gust limit — alongside a 23 mph sustained wind cap — for flying giant balloons at the Thanksgiving Day Parade. Related : How Niche Insurance Shielded Bad Bunny From Bad Weather Those limits were established after the 1997 parade, when gusts over 40 mph slammed The Cat in the Hat balloon into a lamppost on Central Park West.

item.title: Australian Regulator Finds More Suspected Audit Misconduct at Big Four Firms
item.description: Australia’s corporate regulator said on Wednesday it has discovered dozens of additional cases of suspected audit misconduct among the Big Four accounting firms, ranging from misuse of client information to falsified work. The Australian government is considering breaking up the Big Four firms and imposing partnership size caps as well as stipulating a mandatory rotation of audit firms in a bid to clean up the sector. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said it was now considering its enforcement and regulatory options following its review of 558 audit complaints at KPMG, PwC, Deloitte and EY.

item.title: Army Detonates Hazardous Material in Iowa Despite Outcry
item.description: The Army blew up five tons of hazardous materials stored at a facility in Iowa, proceeding with the move despite concerns from US lawmakers and environmental groups that the open-air detonation risked sending a plume of lead dust over surrounding communities a day before Thanksgiving. On X, the Army had said it would proceed with a “controlled, mitigated detonation” at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Despite concerns about contamination, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals had concluded Monday that the US Environmental Protection Agency had “adequately incorporated safeguards to minimize the dispersal of lead dust into the environment.” “We are committed to the safety and health of the people of this region, and we will do everything in our power to protect them,” Adam Telle, the acting Army secretary, said in a statement on X on Tuesday night.

item.title: Specialist Risk Group to acquire Southall Harries
item.description: Specialist Risk Group (SRG) agreed to acquire Southall Harries, a commercial insurance broker based in Lichfield, near Birmingham. Founded in 2006 by Matt Southall and Marc Harries, the brokerage specializes in fleet and commercial insurance. The acquisition expands SRG’s UK retail broking operations in the Midlands, adding Southall Harries’ commercial client portfolio and fleet insurance expertise.

item.title: Revau acquires Burns & Wilcox Canada
item.description: The Toronto-based operation, which has operated as Burns & Wilcox Canada, will transition to the Revau brand. Brokers that worked with Burns & Wilcox Canada will gain access to Revau’s insurance markets for larger and more complex risks. The acquisition expands Quebec-headquartered Revau’s broker network, particularly in Ontario and Atlantic Canada.

item.title: One Pen targets January launch
item.description: One Pen, a San Diego-based insurance underwriting startup led by Tyler “Ty” Robben, plans to launch in January 2027. The company says experienced underwriters will review every submission and that it will deliver decisions instantly. Its website does not yet identify the insurance lines it plans to write.

item.title: Cytora Adds GBG Identity, Financial Crime Checks to Underwriting Workflows
item.description: (Image source: GBG website.) Cytora (London) has added identity, business-verification and financial-crime screening from GBG (Chester, England) to its commercial-insurance risk workflows. Cytora says the checks are logged as part of the workflow, creating an audit trail around the identity and financial-crime controls applied to each submission. Under the agreement, GBG joins Cytora’s Data Partner Ecosystem as its identity and financial-crime intelligence provider.

item.title: San Francisco Faces Onslaught of Tidal Floods Juiced by El Niño
item.description: Related: Companies’ El Niño Anxiety Is Surging as Weather Perils Loom Water levels around San Francisco are forecast to crest near historic highs each day through Thursday, peaking as much as 2.7 feet (82 centimeters) above normal, according to the National Weather Service. San Francisco’s waterfront is facing a stretch of near-record “king tides” this week, threatening flooding just as Thanksgiving travel picks up across the region. Mayor Daniel Lurie said flood walls near San Francisco’s airport were expected to hold, preventing water from spilling onto the tarmac, though winds of up to 40 miles (64 kilometers) per hour may still disrupt outgoing flights.

item.title: Microsoft Declares ‘Code Red’ After Historic Outage, Internal Memos Show
item.description: Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft’s engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July.

item.title: Waymo Recall Prompted by Several Incidents of Robotaxis Entering Closed Freeway Lanes
item.description: Alphabet-owned Waymo said Tuesday its new recall of nearly 4,500 self-driving vehicles in the US was prompted by 11 incidents of robotaxis entering closed freeway lanes since Oct. On Friday, Reuters first reported Waymo was issuing two recalls for its robotaxis over incidents involving closed freeway lanes and manual traffic control. 9 just three days after the company had “updated the approved scope of operation to reduce exposure to closed freeway lanes.” Waymo said there were no collisions or injuries reported from the closed freeway events, adding it is still working on the recall remedy.

item.title: States Band Together During Holiday Road Safety Initiative
item.description: As part of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s (NHTSA) “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” campaign, law enforcement in both states will deter and intercept impaired drivers during the month of December and into the New Year holiday. During the effort, PSP will offer no-cost child passenger safety seat fitting clinics at several locations statewide, with the goal of keeping Pennsylvania’s youngest travelers safe on the road. Officials from the three states are reminding drivers to use their seatbelts, drive sober, and eliminate distractions behind the wheel this holiday season.

item.title: ESMA proposal to limit cat bonds in UCITS funds leaves investors with greater risk: Plenum’s Grieger
item.description: Building on that critique, Grieger takes aim at ESMA’s risk assessment of catastrophe bond funds in its TRV Risk Monitor 1/2026 , with the manager stressing that ESMA draws attention to retail investor risks it considers particularly concerning, while simultaneously pointing to its proposal to restrict the allocation of catastrophe bonds in UCITS funds to 10%. In a pointed critique of the European Securities and Markets Authority’s (ESMA) push to cap UCITS catastrophe bond allocations at 10%, Daniel Grieger, Managing Partner and Senior Portfolio Manager at Plenum Investments argues that the regulator’s risk assessment relies on isolated loss events while ignoring decades of empirical data and evidence. In the paper, Plenum Investments shared its opinions on the ESMA recommendation, highlighting that catastrophe bonds are a mature asset class that has been successfully integrated into UCITS over a long period of time.

item.title: MS Amlin syndicate gets upsized $150m aggregate retro from Kanata Re 2026-1 cat bond
item.description: The $150 million tranche of Kanata Re 2026-1 Class A notes will provide Syndicate 2001 and sub-entities with protection on an annual aggregate and industry loss index trigger basis, while the covered perils and regions will include U.S. Lloyd’s syndicate 2001, which is aligned with Mitsui Sumitomo underwriting entity MS Amlin, has now priced and secured its first catastrophe bond, with the Arthur Re Ltd. – Kanata Re 2026-1 transaction set to provide an upsized $150 million of multi-peril and multi-regional retrocession, Artemis can report.

item.title: Allied World secures upsized $375m 2001 CAT Re 2026-1 cat bond at reduced pricing
item.description: Allied World Assurance Company (AWAC) has now successfully finalised its third and largest catastrophe bond to secure an upsized $375 million of annual aggregate retrocession from the new 2001 CAT Re Ltd. Allied World Assurance Company, part of the Fairfax Financial group, returned to the catastrophe bond earlier this month for a renewal and expansion of its protection, given that the firm’s $275 million 2001 CAT Re 2023-1 cat bond is set to mature at the end of this year. In our second update, Allied World kept the $375 million upsized target, but lowered the pricing again for each of the three tranches of notes on offer, as the insurance and reinsurance firm looked to further capitalise on market conditions to lock-in well-priced aggregate protection.

item.title: Lower reinsurance costs support improving returns for US homeowners insurers: Aon
item.description: Lower reinsurance costs are helping US homeowners insurers improve underwriting margins and prospective returns on equity (ROE), although catastrophe exposure continues to constrain profitability, according to global insurance and reinsurance broker and risk advisory firm Aon. According to Aon, lower reinsurance costs can improve net underwriting margins for catastrophe-exposed homeowners insurers, while enhanced protection can reduce earnings volatility and the capital required to support catastrophe risk. In its latest Homeowners Return on Equity Outlook report, Aon highlighted that increased reinsurance capacity and stronger reinsurer appetite contributed to double-digit reductions in risk-adjusted catastrophe excess-of-loss reinsurance pricing across the broader US property market at the midyear 2026 renewals.

item.title: Applied Systems acquires InsurTech Tailwind
item.description: Applied Systems, a global provider of cloud-based software for the insurance industry, has acquired Tailwind, a document and data retrieval InsurTech company, to accelerate integrated artificial intelligence (AI) automation across the assembly line of insurance. Through Tailwind’s AI-powered technology, Applied aims to further automate the retrieval of carrier documents and their intake into its management systems. As part of Applied, Tailwind will accelerate delivery across the three core domains of the Epic Conductor AI platform: operational AI automation, financial AI automation, and connected AI trading.

item.title: WTW appoints Natalie Kenny as North America Builder’s Risk Broking Leader
item.description: WTW, a global advisory, broking and solutions company specialising in people, risk and capital, has announced the promotion of Natalie Kenny to North America Builder’s Risk Broking Leader, based in New York. Since joining Willis in 2022, Kenny has contributed to the expansion of the company’s builder’s risk business across North America. In her new role, Kenny will collaborate with WTW’s regional, industry, advocacy and production teams to strengthen client relationships and further develop the company’s builder’s risk insurance capabilities throughout North America.

item.title: Tornado Hits Parts of South Florida Following Days of Heavy Rain
item.description: An EF-1 tornado caused damage in Delray Beach and Boca Raton but no injuries, marking one of the latest storms that have plagued much of Florida in the last two weeks. That was preceded by massive amounts of rainfall that caused flooding in parts of Florida’s east coast over the past few weeks. Topics Catastrophe Florida Natural Disasters Windstorm

item.title: Police Investigating if Titans’ Football Player Assaulted Lyft Driver Before Crash
item.description: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Florida following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a ride-share driver. Tampa police said in a statement that Harrell was a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento “when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion.” The driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and struck a second vehicle before colliding with a utility pole. “We have permanently banned the rider’s account from the Lyft platform, reached out to the driver to offer our support, and stand ready to assist law enforcement with an investigation.” The 24-year-old Harrell has not played for the Titans this season.

item.title: Australia Bolsters Online Safety Law With Tougher Big Tech Fine
item.description: Wells described the legislation as Australia’s most significant step yet to improve online safety. The sweeping legislation seeks to reduce online harm by compelling digital service providers from social media platforms to AI chatbots to build safety into their products. Wells said in an interview last month that she wants to use the legislation as a step toward working with other countries and establish basic online safety standards, particularly for children.

item.title: Aviva launches Lifetime Pet Insurance via MoneySuperMarket
item.description: Calum Weston, Managing Director, Pet at Aviva, said: "By launching through price comparison websites initially, we can meet customers where they’re already shopping for pet cover, bringing Aviva’s trusted brand to an important channel for customers comparing pet insurance." Sara Newell, Commercial Director at MoneySuperMarket, said: "We’re delighted to partner with Aviva to offer its new Lifetime Pet Insurance exclusively through MoneySuperMarket. Aviva has launched Lifetime Pet Insurance for cats and dogs. The product is sold initially exclusively through MoneySuperMarket, before expanding to other major price comparison websites during 2027.

item.title: BrokerLink acquires two Alberta insurance brokerages
item.description: BrokerLink , a subsidiary of Intact Financial Corporation, acquired two Alberta insurance brokerages in early November. Calgary-based Touchstone Insurance joined on November 1, followed by Medicine Hat-based Reliance Insurance Agencies on November 2. It offers an exclusive course-of-construction insurance program and specialized coverage for churches and charities.

item.title: Supertake raises $20 million
item.description: AI investing startup Supertake has closed a $20 million seed round led by Adjacent, with backing from Union Square Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Nat Friedman, Nikita Bier, Scott Belsky, Guillermo Rauch, Nemil Dalal, and more. Founded in 2026, Supertake allows people to turn their beliefs into investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents. Users can connect their brokerage accounts (Coinbase and Robinhood for now) and explain what they believe in, and Supertake’s AI turns it into an investment portfolio.

item.title: Primerica authorizes $500 million share buyback for 2027
item.description: Primerica announced that its board authorized up to $500 million in common stock repurchases through December 31, 2027. At year-end 2025, Primerica insured more than 5.5 million lives and had about 3.1 million client investment accounts. The board can end the program at any time, and Primerica is under no obligation to repurchase shares.
